issues.description: URL construction complects parsing, arch extraction, and path templating into one loop
issues.detail: use_koji_url_only braids three concerns: deciding if a URL is already coreos-pool, parsing NEVRA from the tail, and synthesizing a koji path. The 'value' here is a package coordinate (name, version, release, arch); the code never names it. Extract a parse_nevra() returning that value, then a render_koji_url(value) pure function. The loop becomes one map over values.

issues.description: nevra[0].lower() treats a filename string as if it were a parsed identity
issues.detail: The koji path uses the first character of the NEVRA filename as a directory shard. That works only because filenames happen to begin with the package name. The code is reaching into a string as if it were structured data. If the package value were parsed once (name, ver, rel, arch), the shard would be name[0].lower() and the intent would be visible. Right now it is incidental.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url returning None is silently swallowed downstream
issues.detail: extract_arch_from_url returns None on no match, and the caller interpolates it into an f-string producing '/latest/None/Packages'. Value and absence-of-value are complected with string formatting. Either raise on no match, or model the result as a tagged value the caller must handle. A broken URL written into rpms.lock.yaml will fail far from here.

issues.description: Hard-coded koji base URL and arch list are configuration masquerading as code
issues.detail: koji_url_base and the arches list are facts about the world (where coreos-pool lives, which arches we support) embedded inside a function. They are values; they belong as module-level constants or, better, passed in. This is easy (close at hand) but not simple: changing the koji host now requires editing function bodies in two places.

issues.description: Race between lockfile commit and koji tagging is essential complexity hidden in a comment
issues.detail: The PR description acknowledges the URL is crafted before coreos-koji-tagger actually tags the build. That is a real time-semantics problem: the lockfile asserts a fact (this URL resolves) that becomes true only after a separate async system acts. The code should at minimum verify the URL or record the expected tag time as a value, not assume eventual consistency silently.

issues.description: Dead prioritization logic left in query_packages_location after approach change
issues.detail: The 'coreos-pool' preference in query_packages_location is now redundant: use_koji_url_only rewrites every non-pool URL anyway. The earlier branch is now incidental complexity preserved out of caution. Either remove it or state plainly why both layers exist. Two mechanisms doing related work is exactly the complecting this refactor was meant to undo.

review.summary: The patch trades one DNF5 workaround for another, and the new one is easy (a small diff close to the existing code) but not simple. The real value flowing through is a package coordinate (name, version, release, arch) and the real identity is "where coreos-pool will host this NEVRA after tagging" — neither is named. Instead, strings are parsed by index, arches by regex, and absence-of-arch by None, with the koji path templated inline. The essential complexity worth keeping explicit is the race between lockfile commit and koji tag; the incidental complexity is the URL-as-string manipulation. Decompose into parse_nevra, render_koji_url, and a top-level map; then the race becomes the only hard question left.
